newsitem.title: CHINA: China launches first joint venture foreign trade company.
newsitem.headline: China launches first joint venture foreign trade company.

text.p: China has launched the first joint venture foreign trade company in the Pudong New Area of Shanghai, the Shanghai Securities News said on Friday.

An agreement was signed between China's Shanghai Lansheng Co and South Korea's Daewoo Corp to set up the joint venture Lansheng Daewoo Co, the newspaper said. The new firm still requires Beijing's approval, it said.
The newspaper quoted a spokesman for the new company as saying that the joint venture was expected to have a trade turnover of $5 billion by the year 2000.
China's President Jiang Zeming promised at an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting in 1995 Beijing would lift a ban and allow establishment of joint venture foreign trade firms.

In September this year, the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation issued a set of rules on such joint ventures, saying Beijing would allow trial firms first only in Shanghai's Pudong New Area and southern city of Shenzhen.

Shanghai Lansheng is a major Chinese foreign trade company with a foreign trade turnover of $450 million in 1995 and Daewoo, one of the world's 100 biggest enterprises, had a sales turnover of $51.2 billion in 1995, the newspaper said.
